content.title: About
content.content: Arugula (Eruca vesicaria) is a leafy vegetable with a distinct slightly bitter, nutty flavor. It is cultivated in temperate regions and is commonly used fresh in salads, as a garnish, or in mixed greens.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Arugula belongs to the Brassicaceae family, the same as cabbage, broccoli, and mustard.
It was already grown in ancient Rome, where it was prized for its aroma and medicinal properties.
The leaves are rich in glucosinolates, which break down into compounds with potential anti‑cancer effects.
In Italy arugula is often called "rocket" because of the shape of its leaves.
Harvest season is spring and autumn, when the leaves are most tender and flavorful.

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains vitamin A and carotenoids
items.content: Support vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is needed for DNA synthesis and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Low‑calorie source of fiber
items.content: Helps regulate digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Glucosinolates and polyphenols protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to arugula.

items.title: Thyroid concerns
items.content: High amounts of glucosinolates can affect thyroid function when consumed in excess.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: As with any fresh produce, wash arugula thoroughly to remove possible bacteria and pesticide residues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Arugula is enjoyed raw in salads, tossed with olive oil, lemon juice, nuts, and cheeses. It can also be added to sandwiches, pastas, pizza after baking, or quickly sautéed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store arugula in the refrigerator in a bag or container with a slight moisture layer. Use within 3–5 days. Discard if leaves turn yellow or develop an off odor.
